teams.heading: Fiji's interest in Mark Nawaqanitawase stays open; Les Kiss waits to year-end
teams.body: Mark Nawaqanitawase, the former Wallabies winger with 11 Test caps, is eligible for Fiji, Italy and Australia after his three-year stand-down, and was reported to be weighing a switch before his return to union. Fiji Rugby chief executive Koli Sewabu says the governing body is following developments with interest and would support whatever decision the player makes. Wallabies head coach Les Kiss says he will wait until the end of the year to see where the player sits.

teams.heading: England women met Canada in Toronto on Friday, before an expected 18,000
teams.body: England women played third-ranked Canada in Toronto on Friday, a fixture billed as the most-anticipated home rugby match in Canada's history. Canada were looking to avenge their 2025 Women's Rugby World Cup final defeat to No. 1-ranked England, with an expected 18,000 fans at BMO Field. Paige DeNeve, a former Brock University rugby star, said a Canada win would be historic.

lead.why: The men's ranking story is already in today's edition, and the rugby league item is not England's rugby union team, so the women's Toronto test is the strongest remaining new item.

teams.heading: Wallabies could overtake France in world rankings with Bledisloe win
teams.body: France sit fourth in the World Rugby men's rankings on 87.43 points, but the second Bledisloe Test in Sydney could take that place away. Australia, sixth after a 50-19 defeat at Eden Park, would climb above Les Bleus into fourth with a win over New Zealand by more than 15 points, ending a 12-match losing run against the All Blacks. A narrower win would leave France in fourth.

lead.why: The Bledisloe result could cost France fourth place in the world rankings, and it is the only shortlist item with a France stake that is not already in the reader's recent editions.

teams.heading: Steven Kitshoff recalls Springboks' Paris bar fury at Finn Russell's jibe
teams.body: Steven Kitshoff, the retired Springbok prop, recalls in his memoir Kitsie how a Paris bar encounter with Scotland's Finn Russell turned personal. Springbok teammate Franco Mostert told Springbok coach Jacques Nienaber about Russell's jibe about beating the Springbok defence, and Kitshoff says Russell's manner towards teammate Handré Pollard was what pushed the squad over the edge. The book also explains why South Africa's rivalry with Ireland flared after a 2017 loss in Dublin.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item on the shortlist, and its Russell bar episode is a distinct anecdote from the Etzebeth claim already reported.

teams.heading: Dafydd Jenkins says Wales's English-based players can strengthen Welsh game
teams.body: Exeter lock Dafydd Jenkins says the growing number of Wales players in the English Premiership can strengthen the game at home. The 23-year-old, who has spent his whole senior career at Sandy Park, believes the exposure opens space for younger hookers and back-rowers in the URC regions. Wales captains Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake moved from Ospreys to Gloucester this summer, and Jenkins admitted he was 'pretty gutted' after their opening-day win over Exeter Chiefs.

lead.why: Wales international Dafydd Jenkins speaks on the Welsh game's English-based players, a fresh Wales-angled story that doesn't repeat the Thomas, Wainwright-trio or Faletau items already run.

teams.heading: Spain tipped as front-runner against Argentina's South American 2035 World Cup bid
teams.body: Argentina's South American bid for the 2035 World Cup now faces a rival: one report makes Spain front-runner, with a Nou Camp final in its pitch. The four-nation bid, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Brazil, would all host matches, and World Rugby is expected to name its preferred hosts in May 2027. World Rugby's council decides in November. Félix Páez Molina, president of the Argentine rugby union, called the candidacy "a very important step for Argentine rugby and the whole region."

teams.heading: Wallabies could climb to fifth in rankings with a Bledisloe II win
teams.body: A win over New Zealand in Sydney would lift the Wallabies from sixth to fifth on World Rugby's men's rankings, passing England (85.68) who sit fifth in the latest table, against Australia's 84.89. A win by more than 15 points would send coach Les Kiss' side north ranked fourth, above France. A second All Blacks win would see Australia slip to seventh, swapping places with Scotland.

lead.why: It is a new, Australia-specific stake that the rankings permutations make concrete, and it is not a repeat of the Kiss selection story already run.

teams.heading: New Zealand Rugby loses early round of Chiefs name fight with ARLC
teams.body: New Zealand Rugby's bid for an interim injunction against the Australian Rugby League Commission over the Chiefs name has been declined by the High Court in Wellington. Justice Karen Grau accepted the ARLC's assurances on geo-blocking social media content for the PNG club's launch, and the court will give its reasons next week. NZR's lawyer Earl Gray had warned that the PNG Chiefs' launch would entrench the name, but the trademark dispute is far from over, with a full court hearing due early next year.

lead.why: It is the strongest new hard news in the pack: a High Court ruling against New Zealand Rugby, with the principal named and the dispute still live.

teams.heading: Lions lock Hyron Andrews found dead in France before Champions Cup match
teams.body: Johannesburg-based Lions lock Hyron Andrews, 31, was found dead on Friday at a hotel on the Île de Ré, off western France, on the eve of the club's Champions Cup match against La Rochelle. Local authorities have opened an investigation, with accidental death the leading line of inquiry and an autopsy due. Andrews had returned to South Africa this year after two seasons at Sale Sharks, and had represented his country at under-20 level. The Lions say the fixture will go ahead as planned, in his honour.
